authoredPrompt: This figure shows a single curved surface patch sigma_k in 3D space, illustrating the geometric meaning of the integrand in the surface flux integral. The patch sigma_k is depicted as a curved tile (teal) with its area labeled Delta_Sk; a unit normal vector n (purple arrow, pointing upward) is drawn at the center of the patch, and black arrows along the sides indicate the direction of fluid flow passing through the surface. A caption box connected to the patch reads: The volume of fluid crossing sigma_k in the direction of n per unit of time. The figure illustrates that the quantity F(x*_k, y*_k, z*_k) dot n(x*_k, y*_k, z*_k) Delta_Sk approximates the volume of fluid passing through the patch in the normal direction per unit time, motivating the Riemann sum definition of the flux integral.
authoredInteractions:
- Drag the surface patch σₖ to different locations on the full surface and watch the outward normal vector n reorient and the patch area ΔSₖ update
- Slider for flow velocity magnitude: show how the volume of fluid crossing the patch in the direction of n per unit time scales proportionally

discrepancies: A large wireframe hemisphere is drawn which does not exist in the source figure.
The large beige text box and block arrow pointing to the volume are missing from the 3D visualization.
The magenta normal arrow points radially outwards, whereas in the source it points straight up parallel to the side arrows.
Leader lines connecting the labels to the surface and area are missing.
evaluation.notes: The figure successfully implements the mathematical concept with useful interactivity, but deviates significantly from the source's visual composition by embedding the patch in a distracting hallucinated wireframe hemisphere.
action_items: Remove the wireframe sphere geometry and base circle so the patch stands alone as in the original figure.
Change the normal vector 'n' to point straight up to match the visual representation in the source figure, or ensure the extrusion direction exactly matches the normal vector.
Add the large text box and beige block arrow pointing to the volume within the 3D scene or as a closely integrated HTML overlay.
Add curved lines to connect the 'Area' and 'Surface' labels to their respective parts of the geometry.
